what: Prepare the data and fit a model
title: Introduction to Creating Forest Plots for Bayesian Meta Analyses
code: library(metafor) library(brms) library(bayesfoRest)  # Compute log odds ratios with {metafor} binary_es <- escalc(   measure = "OR",   ai = Event_Intervention, bi = Outcome_Intervention_No,   ci = Event_Control, di = Outcome_Control_No,   n1i = N_Intervention, n2i = N_Control,   data = binary_outcome) |>   dplyr::mutate(sei = sqrt(vi))  # Fit a random-effect meta-analysis with brms model_bin <- brm(   yi | se(sei) ~ 1 + (1 | Author),   family = gaussian(),   data = binary_es,   prior = prior(normal(0, 1), class = Intercept) +           prior(cauchy(0, 0.5), class = sd),   iter = 4000,   cores = parallel::detectCores(),   control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),   silent = 2)

title: Introduction to Creating Forest Plots for Bayesian Meta Analyses
text: Name columns hold study label, year arm-level data. binary outcome group sizes event counts:  continuous outcome, use mean_ctrl, mean_int, sd_ctrl sd_int place event columns. time--event rate outcomes, use time_ctrl time_int.
code: bayes_forest(   model = model_bin,   data = binary_es,   measure = "OR",   studyvar = Author,   yearvar = Year,   n_ctrl = N_Control,   n_int = N_Intervention,   event_ctrl = Event_Control,   event_int = Event_Intervention,   title = "Treatment Effect on Binary Outcome",   subtitle = "Bayesian Random-Effect Meta-Analysis (Odds Ratio)",   xlim = c(0.1, 3.5) )
